chunks: As for Muhammad ibn Sinan, it is narrated from Ali ibn al-Husayn ibn Dawood who said:

I heard Abu Ja'far, the second (Imam al-Jawad), peace be upon him, mentioning Muhammad ibn Sinan in a good way, saying: 'Allah is pleased with him because I am pleased with him; he did not oppose me, nor did he oppose my father, ever.'

key_terms.بِرِضَايِ عَنْهُ: Because of my pleasure with him
key_terms.مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ سِنَانٍ: Muhammad ibn Sinan, a prominent companion

ai.seo_question: What is the significance of Muhammad ibn Sinan in Shia tradition according to Imam al-Jawad?
ai.summary: This hadith from Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Kitab al-Ghayba* underscores the theological weight of *al-wala'* (loyalty) by linking Muhammad ibn Sinan’s personal piety directly to the Imam’s approval. It serves as a critical criterion for validating the emissaries during the Minor Occultation, emphasizing that consistency with the Imam’s teachings—specifically avoiding deviation from the lineage of al-Kazim and al-Jawad—is the hallmark of true faithfulness.
